newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo minister calls for ban on sugar imports - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo minister calls for ban on sugar imports - paper.

text.p: Yugoslav agriculture minister Tihomir Vrebalov says sugar and meat imports should be severely restricted to protect the local food and cattle industry, Belgrade newspapers reported on Tuesday.

"Hitherto uncontrolled imports of sugar and meat have brought our agricultural and food processing industry into an even more difficult and almost desperate position," Vrebalov was quoted by Nasa Borba as saying.
Yugoslavia imported 180,000 tonnes of refined and raw sugar this year even though it still has around 100,000 tonnes of sugar surplus left over from last year, Vrebalov said.
Sugar output in 1996 sugar was estimated at some 270,000 tonnes.
Vrebalov said the ministry had asked the federal government to "ban" all sugar imports, including previously negotiated deals.
"We should export our surplus to at least partly cover costs of this year's sugar beet production," he said.
Meat imports were also "unnecessary" because there was enough livestock in local farms to cover domestic needs, he said.

The country's meat industry suffered a setback when the European Union banned meat exports from Yugoslavia following an outbreak of hoof-and-mouth disease in the southern province of Kosovo earlier this year.

European Union institutions have told the ministry that all import restrictions on livestock and meat from Yugoslavia will be lifted by November 2, according to Vrebalov. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
